Problem: How to implement a UI screen or page that displays data from multiple services.
Context: You have applied the Microservice architecture pattern. Services are developed by business capability decomposition or subdomain decomposition oriented teams that are also responsible for the user experience. Some UI screens/pages display data from multiple services, where each data item corresponds to a separate service and its display is the responsibility of a different team (e.g., an Amazon-style product detail page displaying basic info, purchase history, availability, buying options, related items, customer reviews, seller ranking from different services).
Solution: Each team develops a web application that generates the HTML fragment implementing the region of the page for their service. A UI team is responsible for developing page templates that build pages by performing serverside aggregation (e.g., serverside include style mechanism) of these service-specific HTML fragments.
Result: A unified UI screen or page is successfully composed from multiple microservices. This approach can minimize client-service roundtrips, serve content to both mobile native apps and mobile web apps, provide a consistent customer experience, and reduce duplicated engineering costs by allowing reuse of modules across pages.
Related Patterns: Clientside UI composition (as an alternative approach).
Uses: Amazon-style product detail pages, eBay's extended implementation for mobile/desktop web apps, and composition of reusable modules like Marketing, Ads, or Merchandising modules.

It also discusses related patterns and provides real-world examples of its application.
